parts.text: (a) Calcium oxide is made by the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate.

ms.label: 5(a)(i)
ms.text:
breakdown of substance / idea of one substance forming two or more substances (1)
using heat / on heating (1)

ms.label: 5(a)(ii)
ms.text:

white precipitate / white solid (1)
OR
add (aqueous) ammonia (1)
no precipitate / very slight white precipitate (1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Carbon dioxide is produced when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate. CaCO 3 + 2HC l → CaC l 2 + CO 2 + H 2 O

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete the diagram to show how to measure the volume of carbon dioxide produced during this reaction. [2]

ms.label: 5(b)(i)
ms.text:
gas syringe / upturned measuring cylinder dipping into container (1)
apparatus is workable and airtight (1)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Describe the effect of each of the following on the rate of reaction of dilute hydrochloric acid with calcium carbonate. ● The concentration of hydrochloric acid is decreased. All other conditions stay the same. ............................................................................................................................................. ● The temperature is increased. All other conditions stay the same. ............................................................................................................................................. [2]

ms.label: 5(b)(ii)
ms.text:
lower concentration of acid: decreases (in rate) / reaction slower / lower rate / slows down (1)
higher temperature: increases (in rate) / reaction faster / higher rate / speeds up (1)
